item.title: Piyush S/O Deepak Narlawar vs State Of Maharashtra on 2 November, 2026
item.description:
NAGARATHNA, J.

Leave granted.

2. This appeal arises out of the order dated 08.01.2025 passed by the Bombay High Court, Aurangabad Bench in Criminal Application No.725/2024 filed under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, “CrPC”) refusing to quash the proceedings qua the appellant arising out of FIR No.212/2023 dated 30.06.2023 registered with Satara Police Station, District Aurangabad Town under Sections 304B, 323, 498A, 504 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, “IPC”) and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short, “DP Act”). However, while dismissing the said criminal application with respect to the appellant herein, the High Court granted the relief of quashing the FIR and all consequential proceedings thereto qua the other family members of the appellant, namely, respondent Nos.3 to 5. Aggrieved, the appellant, who is the son-in-law of the complainant-respondent No.2, has preferred the present criminal appeal.

item.title: Surendra Manjhi vs Union Of India on 2 November, 2026
item.description:
VIKRAM NATH, J.

1. The prohibition of bonded labour is among the most fundamental assurances of human dignity embodied in our Constitution. Freedom from bondage, however, cannot be secured by the act of rescue alone. Unless such freedom is accompanied by timely financial assistance and meaningful rehabilitation, those released from exploitation may find themselves compelled by economic necessity to return to the very conditions from which the law sought to protect them. The obligation of the State, therefore, extends beyond securing their physical liberty to ensuring that such liberty is meaningful, enduring and accompanied by the means to lead a life of dignity.
